nodes.name: Policy Engine
nodes.purpose: Serves as the root configuration layer where agencies define the rules of their operations across caregiving and cleaning.
nodes.ux_intent: Like reading a clear, human-readable playbook of how the agency operates, completely abstracted from database schemas.
nodes.vertical_notes: Centralizes rules for two distinct but related verticals: high-trust caregiving (DBS, First Aid, Paediatrics) and logistics-heavy cleaning (COSHH, territory management).
nodes.case_integration: Provides the foundational rule-set that governs how cases in the Portfolio app are instantiated and routed.

nodes.name: Credential Taxonomy
nodes.purpose: Manages the universe of acceptable qualifications, background checks, and certifications required for workers.
nodes.ux_intent: A visually organized library of badges and certificates the agency recognizes, feeling like an achievement board.
nodes.vertical_notes: Crucial for capturing the expiry dynamics of DBS checks, Ofsted registrations, and specialized cleaning certificates (e.g., Carpet Cleaning).
nodes.case_integration: Cases will block assignment if workers do not meet the credential taxonomy requirements defined here.

nodes.name: Create Credential Type
nodes.purpose: Allows admins to define a new credential type with its specific validation rules, expiry cadence, and issuing authority.
nodes.ux_intent: Admins feel like they are creating a new 'badge' of honor; they just enter the name and how long it lasts, and the system handles the rest.
nodes.vertical_notes: Examples: 'Enhanced DBS' (requires 3-year expiry check), 'Paediatric First Aid' (3 years), 'COSHH' (1 year).

nodes.name: Update Credential Type
nodes.purpose: Modifies the rules or metadata of an existing credential type, such as extending its default validity period.
nodes.ux_intent: A simple inline edit that instantly updates the compliance rules across the entire agency without creating anxiety about breaking things.
nodes.vertical_notes: If the government changes DBS renewal recommendations, admins can update the rule here and trigger re-evaluations.

nodes.name: Delete Credential Type
nodes.purpose: Archives or removes a credential requirement from the system when it is no longer relevant.
nodes.ux_intent: A gentle 'archive' action that hides the credential from future use without breaking historical compliance records.
open_questions: Should this strictly be a soft-delete to preserve historical worker data?
nodes.vertical_notes: Useful if a specific local qualification is replaced by a national standard.

nodes.name: List Credential Types
nodes.purpose: Fetches the active taxonomy of credentials configured for the agency.
nodes.ux_intent: Instant, heavily cached read operation that powers dropdowns and compliance dashboards effortlessly.
nodes.vertical_notes: Workers see this list during onboarding (e.g., 'Upload your NVQ Level 3').

nodes.name: Set Service Credential Requirements
nodes.purpose: Maps specific credentials as mandatory or recommended for specific service types.
nodes.ux_intent: A visual matrix or drag-and-drop builder: 'To do [Maternity Nursing], a worker must have [Paediatric First Aid]'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Maternity Nurses absolutely require Paediatric First Aid. Commercial Cleaners absolutely require COSHH.
nodes.case_integration: The Case app queries this matrix to validate if an assigned worker is legally compliant for a specific job case.

nodes.name: Service Types
nodes.purpose: Defines the catalog of offerings the agency provides, acting as the structural blueprint for all bookings.
nodes.ux_intent: A clean menu of what the agency sells, focusing on the 'product' rather than the database constraints.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nanny services (Daily, Live-in, Maternity) vs. Cleaning services (Deep clean, Regular domestic, End-of-tenancy).

nodes.name: Create Service Type
nodes.purpose: Adds a new offering to the agency's catalog with base parameters like billing units and minimum durations.
nodes.ux_intent: A wizard that asks 'What do you want to offer?' and 'How do you bill for it?', creating a product instantly.
nodes.vertical_notes: Live-in nanny is billed weekly/monthly. Regular domestic cleaning is billed hourly with a 2-hour minimum.

nodes.name: Update Service Type
nodes.purpose: Modifies parameters of an existing service offering.
nodes.ux_intent: Seamless adjustments without breaking active subscriptions or ongoing jobs.
nodes.vertical_notes: e.g., changing the minimum hours for a 'Deep Clean' from 3 to 4 based on agency feedback.

nodes.name: Archive Service Type
nodes.purpose: Retires a service type so it can no longer be booked, preserving historical data.
nodes.ux_intent: One-click retirement that gracefully warns about any currently active clients on this service.
nodes.vertical_notes: Agency stops offering 'Elderly care' to focus purely on childcare. Archives the service.

nodes.name: List Service Types
nodes.purpose: Retrieves the available service catalog for clients to browse and book.
nodes.ux_intent: Instantaneous load of visually appealing service cards for anonymous or logged-in clients.
nodes.vertical_notes: This powers the main booking flow. Anonymous users see 'What do you need help with? [Nanny] [Cleaning]'.

nodes.name: Set Care Requirements
nodes.purpose: Attaches highly specific vertical rules to a service, such as supported age groups or accommodation needs.
nodes.ux_intent: Toggle switches for 'Requires spare room' (Live-in) or 'Select supported child ages'. Feels like configuring a bespoke product.
nodes.vertical_notes: Live-in nannies MUST have 'requires_live_in_accommodation' set to true. Maternity nurses often apply only to 'Newborns (0-3 months)'.
nodes.case_integration: Case Portfolio reads this to prompt clients to confirm they have a spare room for a live-in nanny.

nodes.name: Matching Strategy Rules
nodes.purpose: Configures the engine that determines how requests are mapped to workers.
nodes.ux_intent: A control panel that lets the admin dial in exactly how automated or bespoke they want their agency to feel.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nanny agencies often use 'shortlist' or 'manual' matching due to high trust requirements. Cleaning uses 'auto-assign' based on proximity.

nodes.name: Set Matching Mode
nodes.purpose: Defines the primary workflow for fulfilling a request: auto-assign, shortlist, portfolio browse, or manual.
nodes.ux_intent: A simple dropdown: 'How should clients get their worker? -> [We auto-assign the best match]'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Emergency nanny = auto-assign. Live-in nanny = shortlist for client to pick. Holiday let clean = auto-assign.
nodes.case_integration: Dictates the state machine path the Case will take when it reaches the matching phase.

nodes.name: Set Sort Weights
nodes.purpose: Configures the algorithmic weighting for scoring worker candidates.
nodes.ux_intent: Sliding scales: 'Prioritize [Distance] vs [Rating] vs [Seniority]'.
nodes.vertical_notes: For cleaning, 'Proximity' weight is cranked up. For nannies, 'Rating' and 'Continuity' are paramount.

nodes.name: Set Continuity Preference
nodes.purpose: Configures how strongly the system should attempt to assign the exact same worker to a recurring client.
nodes.ux_intent: A toggle: 'Always try to send the same person to a regular client'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Crucial for both regular domestic cleaners and regular after-school nannies to build trust.
nodes.case_integration: Cases explicitly flag when continuity is broken, requiring admin or client approval.

nodes.name: Set Proximity Radius
nodes.purpose: Defines the maximum allowed travel distance/time for workers based on their declared zones.
nodes.ux_intent: A simple slider: 'Workers shouldn't travel more than [X] miles/minutes'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Cleaners often operate in strict hyper-local zones (e.g., 5-mile radius). Live-in nannies have zero proximity bounds.

nodes.name: Availability Rules
nodes.purpose: Defines the rules governing how and when workers can be booked and how they manage their own time.
nodes.ux_intent: Setting the heartbeat of the agency's operational capacity.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nannies declare hours. Cleaners declare specific days/shifts. Both need break/leave rules.

nodes.name: Set Booking Window
nodes.purpose: Configures how far in advance, or how late, clients can book a service.
nodes.ux_intent: Simple dropdowns: 'Allow bookings up to [6 months] in advance'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Emergency nannies might have a 2-hour minimum notice. Deep cleans might require 48 hours notice.
nodes.case_integration: Case creation fails immediately if requested outside the valid window.

nodes.name: Define Break Types
nodes.purpose: Configures the allowed statuses for workers to pause their availability.
nodes.ux_intent: Creating understandable reasons for absence: 'Sick Leave', 'Maternity', 'Seasonal Break'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Cleaners often take 'Seasonal Breaks' over holidays. Nannies might take 'Maternity Leave'.

nodes.name: Set Minimum Notice
nodes.purpose: Configures the minimum notice period required for workers to accept a booking.
nodes.ux_intent: Setting boundaries to respect worker time, feeling like an agency that cares about its staff.
nodes.vertical_notes: Emergency bookings bypass this with high pay. Standard cleans require 24 hours.

nodes.name: Payment Rules
nodes.purpose: Defines the financial engine of the agency, determining cuts, premiums, and allowances.
nodes.ux_intent: A straightforward financial dashboard. 'We take X%, they take Y%'. No hidden complex logic.
nodes.vertical_notes: Crucial for handling agency margins, which vary wildly between one-off deep cleans and permanent live-in nanny placements.

nodes.name: Set Agency Split
nodes.purpose: Defines the percentage or fixed fee the agency takes from the total invoice.
nodes.ux_intent: A simple slider or text box: 'Agency Fee: 15%'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Live-in nannies often involve a large upfront finder's fee (e.g., 4 weeks pay), while daily cleaners are a standard % split on hourly rate.
nodes.case_integration: Directly influences the financial ledgers generated per Case.

nodes.name: Set Overtime Rules
nodes.purpose: Configures multipliers for hours worked beyond the standard limit.
nodes.ux_intent: A rule builder: 'If hours > 8 per day, multiply rate by 1.5'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Common in nannying where parents are delayed. Cleaners rarely use overtime, they just add flat extra time.
nodes.case_integration: Calculates final invoice in Case when worker checks out later than scheduled.

nodes.name: Set Emergency Premium
nodes.purpose: Configures surcharges for bookings made with extremely short notice.
nodes.ux_intent: A toggle: 'Charge an extra £20 for same-day bookings to incentivize workers'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Emergency nanny cover always triggers this. Passed largely to the worker to secure acceptance.

nodes.name: Set Travel Allowance
nodes.purpose: Configures whether and how workers are compensated for travel time or distance.
nodes.ux_intent: A checkbox: 'Compensate travel over 10 miles at 45p/mile'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Vital for rural cleaners. Nannies usually don't get travel pay unless driving kids during the shift (expense, not travel-to-work).

nodes.name: Set Late Payment Policy
nodes.purpose: Defines penalties and grace periods for unpaid client invoices.
nodes.ux_intent: Automated bad-cop: 'System will automatically add a 5% fee after 7 days overdue'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Protects agencies dealing with long-term caregiving clients who might forget weekly invoices.
nodes.case_integration: Suspends future Cases for the client if threshold is breached.

nodes.name: Set Holiday Pay Accrual
nodes.purpose: Configures how holiday pay is accrued for long-term PAYE workers.
nodes.ux_intent: Ensures legal compliance silently in the background. Admin just clicks 'Enable standard 12.07% accrual'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Permanent nannies often require this. Contractor cleaners do not.

nodes.name: Escalation Rules
nodes.purpose: Defines the triggers and routing for when things go wrong (e.g., worker no-show, client complaint).
nodes.ux_intent: Setting the agency's safety net: 'If nobody accepts the job in 2 hours, text the manager'.
nodes.vertical_notes: In caregiving, a no-show is a critical incident requiring immediate phone escalation. In cleaning, it's an annoyance.

nodes.name: Create Escalation Rule
nodes.purpose: Creates a specific trigger-action pair for anomalous events.
nodes.ux_intent: If-This-Then-That style builder. 'IF worker is 15 mins late THEN alert admin'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Trigger: 'worker_not_checked_in', Threshold: '+15 mins'.

nodes.name: Update Escalation Rule
nodes.purpose: Modifies an existing escalation pathway.
nodes.ux_intent: Easily dial back noise if admins are getting too many alerts for minor delays.
nodes.vertical_notes: Changing 'alert admin at 15 mins' to 'alert admin at 30 mins'.

nodes.name: Delete Escalation Rule
nodes.purpose: Removes an escalation trigger.
nodes.ux_intent: One-click removal of a noisy or outdated alert.
nodes.vertical_notes: Removing an alert that fires every time a cleaner finishes early.

nodes.name: Evaluate Escalation Rules
nodes.purpose: Background job that constantly checks state against rules to fire escalations.
nodes.ux_intent: The invisible guardian that ensures no case falls through the cracks.
nodes.vertical_notes: Evaluates if a nanny is late for school pickup.

nodes.name: Communication Cadence
nodes.purpose: Defines when and how the system communicates with clients and workers automatically.
nodes.ux_intent: Setting the voice and rhythm of the agency. 'Send a polite reminder 24h before'.
nodes.vertical_notes: High touch for nanny trials. Automated and brief for regular weekly cleaning.

nodes.name: Create Communication Rule
nodes.purpose: Sets up an automated message trigger.
nodes.ux_intent: Like a simple marketing automation tool: 'Send SMS to Client 1 hour before job start'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nanny intro profiles are emailed 48hrs before. Cleaner ETAs are SMS'd 1hr before.

nodes.name: Update Communication Rule
nodes.purpose: Modifies the timing, channel, or template of an automated message.
nodes.ux_intent: Quickly adjust the tone or timing if clients report being spammed.
nodes.vertical_notes: Switching from Email to SMS for cleaner ETA reminders due to better open rates.

nodes.name: Delete Communication Rule
nodes.purpose: Stops an automated message from sending in the future.
nodes.ux_intent: Silent removal of a notification layer.
nodes.vertical_notes: Removing 'post-job feedback' request for every single regular clean to avoid annoyance.

nodes.name: Quality Thresholds
nodes.purpose: Defines what constitutes acceptable worker performance and automates consequences for dipping below it.
nodes.ux_intent: Setting the quality bar: 'If a worker drops below 4 stars, auto-suspend them pending review'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Caregivers have zero-tolerance for punctuality issues. Cleaners might have a slightly higher tolerance for minor delays.

nodes.name: Set Quality Threshold
nodes.purpose: Configures a specific metric limit that triggers an action.
nodes.ux_intent: Simple rule creation: 'Metric: Average Rating, Operator: < 4.0, Action: Flag for Review'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Thresholds on 'Client Complaints', 'Late Check-ins', 'Cancelled Shifts'.

nodes.name: Evaluate Quality Thresholds
nodes.purpose: Runs after assignments to update worker scores and trigger actions if thresholds are breached.
nodes.ux_intent: Invisible accountant tracking everyone's performance and surfacing only the anomalies.
nodes.vertical_notes: If a nanny gets a 1-star review for safety, auto-suspend immediately.
nodes.case_integration: Reads assignment completion payload directly from the Case.

nodes.name: Replacement Rules
nodes.purpose: Configures the logic for handling broken continuity or worker unavailability for long-term/recurring jobs.
nodes.ux_intent: Defining the 'recovery strategy' so the agency feels resilient and proactive.
nodes.vertical_notes: If the Tuesday cleaner is sick, do we automatically send a sub, or do we ask the client first? Cleaners usually auto-sub. Nannies usually require client permission.

nodes.name: Set Replacement Policy
nodes.purpose: Configures auto-substitution behaviors based on service type.
nodes.ux_intent: Dropdown: 'When a worker cancels: [Auto-find replacement] / [Ask client]'.
nodes.vertical_notes: Nanny: Ask client ('Mary is sick, would you like us to send Jane?'). Cleaner: Auto-sub ('Mary is sick, Jane is covering your clean today').
nodes.case_integration: Directs the branching logic when a Case assignment is cancelled by the worker.
